text:
jess: Quick flag on PR #5780 — a couple of subtle but test-breaking mismatches in api-ref and SDK snippets. TL;DR: inconsistent `request_id` casing in examples/headers, and pagination example uses `cursor` vs `next_token` and mixes null vs empty-string. CI snippet-verify is failing because the generated OpenAPI client types don't match the examples.

omar: Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5780. The failing test shows the OpenAPI-generated TS client expects response.header `x-request-id` and the examples use `requestId` inside the JSON body as well as `Request-Id` in curl headers. We need to pick a canonical place and casing.

jess: Right now we have three patterns in the docs:
- header: `Request-Id: <uuid>` in curl snippets
- body: `{ "requestId": "..." }` in example responses
- header example in OpenAPI `x-request-id` (lower-kebab)
This divergence breaks the example validator and confuses SDK generation.

leigh: My proposal: canonicalize on `x-request-id` header (kebab-case) for transport, and DO NOT embed it in response body examples. If we want to show the request id in examples, include a short note saying "the server also sets `X-Request-Id` header" instead of duplicating it into JSON. That keeps OpenAPI and runtime aligned.

omar: Strong +1. I'll update api-ref/common.yaml to add a reusable header parameter `X-Request-Id` and add a small docs note. Also update all curl snippets to use `-H "X-Request-Id: $REQ_ID"` and remove `requestId` from example response blocks.

jess: Another related problem: pagination. Some guides show `cursor: ""` to indicate no next page, others show `next_token: null`, and the OpenAPI schema marks `next_token` as nullable string. The TypeScript generator treats nullable string differently than an empty string so tests that assert types fail.

leigh: Can we standardize on `next_token` (nullable) and examples should omit the field when there is no next page? That fits OpenAPI nullable semantics and results in cleaner generated types. Also add a small migration note in guides/pagination.md explaining legacy `cursor` aliases.

omar: I'll change examples in api-ref endpoints that return paginated lists (search, list-models, logs) to use `next_token` and omit it on the final page. I'll add YAML comments for maintainers explaining the decision.

jess: One more oddity: embeddings and rerank response examples in a few community guides include a top-level `meta` object with `usage` counters (tokens/latency). Our runtime returns `usage` as a sibling field to `data` in the body, not nested under `meta`. The OpenAPI schema models `usage` at top-level. Those docs cause the snippet-verify to fail because shape mismatch is strict.

leigh: Please normalize those to the canonical shape: `{ "data": [...], "usage": { "tokens": 12 }, "model":"..." }`. And add a short note that older examples from community-contrib might use `meta.usage` — we've migrated to top-level `usage`.

omar: Will sweep community-contrib examples and make PRs where necessary. For user-facing changelog, I'll add one line under docs/changes.md about request id header + pagination canonicalization with snip-121 reference.

jess: Small tooling ask: can we add a unit in snippet-linter that detects `requestId` or `Request-Id` present inside example JSON bodies and flags them (snip-122)? That will prevent accidental reintroductions. Also add a lint rule to flag `cursor` field usage in response examples unless it's inside a legacy section.

ci-bot: snippet-runner queued for PR 5780 (approx ETA 12m)

omar: Pushed the initial patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/commit/e7f9c2c — removed `requestId` from response examples, added X-Request-Id header param in api-ref/common.yaml, converted paginated examples to `next_token` and omitted it when empty, and updated docs/changes.md. Left TODO comment in api-ref/routing.md about updating old community samples.

leigh: I'll run the snippet-linter locally after your push. Also, please add a one-line comment in api-ref OpenAPI examples to clarify that examples omit `next_token` when there is no next page; that will save future authors.

omar: Done. Committed a follow-up with the linter rule added (snip-122) and a short section in CONTRIBUTING.md.

jess: Awesome. Merged. Thanks team. If anyone spots `requestId` or `cursor` in other docs, tag #docs and I'll triage.
